text: Khatia Dekanoidze - If we look at what is happening in Armenia, you will see that the role Georgia had to be the regional leader no longer exists - Georgia is losing this role due to Ivanishvili's crime and the "Anti-Georgian Dream" (06.05.2026, 12:00)

Today, Ivanishvili and the "Anti-Georgian Dream" have caused Georgia to lose its role in long-term peace, development, progress, and economic prosperity. They have deprived the Georgian people of the opportunity for prosperity and wealth, as well as the opportunity for European integration. This is a historical crime," stated Khatia Dekanoidze, one of the leaders of the National Movement.

He congratulated the public on the "liberation of Adjara from the rule of Russia and the despot" 22 years ago on May 6, and noted that this very day marked the beginning of a new chapter in Georgia's history, which signified the region's leadership.

“I congratulate you on one of the most distinguished dates in Georgia's recent history—the return of Adjara to Georgia. Exactly 22 years ago, on May 6, one of the most significant events in Georgia's recent history took place, when Adjara returned to the heart of Georgia, was liberated from Russian rule, liberated from the rule of a despot, and together with President Mikheil Saakashvili, his team, and many fervent patriots, a very important ascent began. And yes, Georgia started a new chapter, which implied regional leadership, development in technology and education, in the context of Eastern European enlargement, and in the context of a strategic partnership with the USA, which was truly our nation's historical mission. This was the day when we transitioned to a completely different state development, and our team truly managed to secure the role of regional leader for Georgia.

Today, Ivanishvili and the ‘Anti-Georgian Dream’ have caused Georgia to lose its role in long-term peace, development, progress, and economic prosperity. They have deprived the Georgian people of the opportunity for prosperity and wealth, and the opportunity for European integration. This is a historical crime, and if we look at what is happening in our neighbor Armenia—and I want to wish them great success—you will see that the role Georgia once had, to be a regional leader and to have many sustainable peace projects, no longer exists. The events unfolding in Armenia in recent days are not just about political support from the EU, USA, or Canada for our neighbors; these are investment projects that truly imply long-term peace.

We had many such projects; among them, Mikheil Saakashvili, who is now a political prisoner, was directly involved in the development and construction of the Batumi Technological University, and I myself am very proud that I participated in the construction of this technological university. This university was meant to truly become one of Georgia's important hubs for education, technology, new communication systems, and the opportunity to transition to a new stage of education. What has been happening in Armenia is not just political support; it is economic support that ensures long-term peace. Everyone who was involved in the most important stages of Georgia's development is today watching how the country is losing this role due to Ivanishvili's crime, due to the ‘Anti-Georgian Dream.’ 400 billion in investment, military-technological cooperation with France and the United States, energy security projects, the most important new corridor that the European Commission, EU, USA, and Canada are now talking about, massive investments that are one of the most important areas for peace, sustainable development, and progress—Georgia is losing all of this,” Dekanoidze stated.
